request.deadline: Three-month staged liquidity deployment after enactment, with monthly reporting; other final delivery deadline not stated in document
deliverables: Shared BTC reserve architecture with transparent safety mechanisms
Composable FIRE and ICE Cardano-native assets
Open-source SDKs and adapters for wallets, DEXs, and DeFi protocols
Always-on dashboards for reserve ratio, asset supply, liquidity health, fee flows, and deployment status
Monthly governance reports and reporting standards
Independent security review, audit, and economic modeling
Legal, compliance, disclosures, treasury reporting, risk documentation, and launch-readiness review
request.recipient: Intersect is proposed as interim fund administrator, subject to confirmation and final agreement; Sundial remains accountable for deployment and delivery coordination with Charms.
request.what: A TreasuryWithdrawals action to fund Alchemy, a Cardano-native Bitcoin treasury protocol and BTCfi infrastructure layer by Sundial Protocol and Charms.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 10,000,000 ada, using an approximate USD 0.20 per ada reference value for an approximately USD 2.0 million planning budget split into two approximately USD 1.0 million pools.

Pool 1 is intended for protocol infrastructure and staged launch liquidity, kept separate from operating spend, deployed in three monthly tranches of approximately USD 250,000, USD 250,000, and USD 500,000.

Pool 2 is intended for delivery, audit, integrations, dashboards, governance reporting, legal/compliance work, and go-to-market execution with itemized planning allocations totaling approximately USD 1.0 million.
Alchemy proposes a shared BTC reserve architecture where FIRE and ICE are backed by the same BTC reserve, with reserve ratio and FIRE price formulas specified in the document.

The system targets an initial 5.0x reserve ratio and defines safety zones above 4.0x, between 2.0x and 4.0x, and below 2.0x that constrain minting, redemption, and risky activity as reserve conditions worsen.

The proposal states that launch liquidity will be treasury-supported and treasury-owned, with profits, yield, and returns generated by the launch liquidity position returned to the Cardano Treasury quarterly.

The proposal states that launch liquidity principal can be returned to the Treasury after Alchemy reaches a 30-day time-weighted average TVL of at least USD 60 million, subject to a formal governance proposal and approval.

The proposal identifies BTC volatility, oracle risk, bridge risk, Charms protocol-layer risk, novel asset risk, delivery risk, and adoption risk, and lists mitigations including audits, economic modeling, dashboards, pause rules, legal/compliance work, reporting, and staged deployment.

The proposal asserts that Cardano currently has little-to-no BTCfi infrastructure and that failure to fund Alchemy would leave Bitcoin-backed structured exposure consolidating on other chains and off-chain markets.

The proposal cites external references for the Alchemy simulator, Strategy Q1 2026 results, Cardano Constitution update, and NCL reference, making some market and governance assertions externally checkable.

summary: The document presents a 10,000,000 ada treasury request for a Cardano BTCfi protocol with separated liquidity and delivery pools, staged deployment, reserve mechanics, reporting, audits, administration controls, and claimed treasury-return mechanisms, while relying partly on proposer assertions for adoption impact and return execution.
